topic: Both tags are required: what each one does and what breaks without it
queries: do I need both tags
what happens if I only install one tag
difference between lead tag and conversion tag
I installed the conversion tag but no sales are tracked
which tag goes on which page
do I need the lead tag on every page
content:
KST needs **both** tags, and they do different jobs on different pages:

| | Lead Tag | Conversion Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Where | Every page | Order confirmation / thank-you page only |
| Job | Reads the `kk` parameter from the Kelkoo click and stores it as `kelkooId` in first-party storage | Reads that stored identifier and sends the completed order to Kelkoo |
| Consent | Requires user consent (marketing/analytics) | No separate consent — Kelkoo Group relies on legitimate interest |
| Script | `leadtag.js` | `ks.js`, driven by the `_kkstrack` variable |

Common failure patterns that follow from this split:

- **Lead Tag only** — visits are identified but no sales are ever reported.
- **Conversion Tag only** — sales are reported but cannot be attributed to a Kelkoo click, because nothing stored the identifier.
- **Lead Tag missing on some pages** — a user who lands on a page without it never gets an identifier stored, so their later purchase is unattributed.
- **Lead Tag blocked by the CMP** — functionally the same as not having it, since it needs consent to store anything.

The Conversion Tag should fire on *every* completed order, not just orders you believe came from Kelkoo — Kelkoo Group applies its own attribution logic afterwards.

topic: Why Kelkoo's sales numbers differ from Google Analytics
queries: why do my Kelkoo numbers differ from Google Analytics
Kelkoo reports more sales than GA
GA and Kelkoo attribution mismatch
is a discrepancy with analytics a tracking bug
my analytics says a different channel got the sale
should the numbers match exactly
content:
A mismatch between Kelkoo Group's reported sales and your analytics platform is expected, and usually not a bug.

**The core reason is attribution methodology.** KST uses *Kelkoo Channel Last Click* over a 30-day window: if a user clicked a Kelkoo ad within the previous 30 days, the sale is attributed to Kelkoo Group even if the user returned via another channel before buying. A cross-channel last-click model in GA would credit that same sale to the later channel. Both are working correctly; they are answering different questions.

**Things that genuinely cause mismatches worth fixing:**

- **Different order identifiers** — the docs recommend passing the *same* order ID to both KST and your analytics platform so records can be lined up.
- **Different order values** — likewise, pass the same value. KST's guidance is to include VAT and shipping in `orderValue`.
- **Partial tracking** — if the Conversion Tag only fires for some orders, KST's totals will be low regardless of attribution.

So: a *directional* difference in which channel gets credit is normal. A large gap in the raw *count* of orders suggests a tracking problem, not an attribution one.

topic: Consent model: why the two tags are treated differently
queries: do I need consent for KST
which tag needs consent
legitimate interest vs consent Kelkoo
how should I configure my cookie banner for Kelkoo
will blocking cookies stop sales tracking
GDPR setup for the two tags
content:
The two tags sit on different legal bases, which is why they are configured differently in a consent tool:

- **Lead Tag — requires consent.** It writes first-party storage (`kelkooId`, `kk_gclid`, `kk_leadtag`, 12 months each), so it must only fire once marketing/analytics consent is given. On Shopify this maps to setting the pixel's permission to *Required Marketing / Analytics*.
- **Conversion Tag — no separate consent.** Kelkoo Group relies on **legitimate interest** for processing the sales data. On Shopify its pixel permission is set to *Not Required*.

Practical consequences:

- A CMP that blocks everything until consent will suppress the Lead Tag, so those users' purchases cannot be attributed — the sale is still reported, just not linked to a Kelkoo click.
- Kelkoo Group is an independent **data controller**, not your processor, and there is no controller-processor relationship between you.
- For **server-to-server**, consent is entirely the merchant's responsibility — it sits outside the normal cookie consent mechanism.

Data is stored in The Netherlands. The DPO contact is dpo@kelkoogroup.com.

topic: PrestaShop 1.6 vs 1.7 vs 8: what actually differs
queries: difference between PrestaShop 1.6 1.7 and 8 installation
which PrestaShop guide do I follow
PrestaShop version differences Kelkoo
svn1 svn2 vs quantity price PrestaShop
does the PrestaShop setup change by version
I followed the wrong PrestaShop guide
content:
The three PrestaShop guides look similar but differ in ways that will silently break tracking if you follow the wrong one.

| | 1.6x | 1.7x | 8 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead Tag file | `themes/custom/header.tpl` | `templates/_partials/head.tpl` | `templates/_partials/head.tpl` |
| Conversion Tag template | `order-confirmation.tpl` | `checkout/_partials/order-confirmation-table.tpl` | `checkout/_partials/order-confirmation-table.tpl` |
| Basket quantity field | `quantity` | `svn1` | `svn1` |
| Basket price field | `price` | `svn2` | `svn2` |
| `{literal}` around merchantInfo | Yes | No | No |
| Basket output | `{$products_json}` | `{$products_json nofilter}` | `{$products_json nofilter}` |
| Express checkout file | n/a | `order-confirmation-table-simple.tpl` | `order-confirmation-table-simple.tpl` |
| Recompile setting menu | Advanced **settings** → Performance | Advanced **parameters** → Performance | Advanced **parameters** → Performance |
| PayPal module steps | Documented | Not documented | Not documented |

The `svn1`/`svn2` naming on 1.7 and 8 is the single most surprising difference — copying a 1.6 snippet into a 1.7 or 8 store gives fields KST does not expect.

All three share: back up files first, enable template recompilation, clear the cache after changes, and remove any old `leadtag.js` / `_kkstrack`. PrestaShop 8's guide additionally warns that **KST must be reinstalled after any PrestaShop or theme upgrade** — worth assuming on every version, since upgrades overwrite the same controller and template files.

topic: Basket field names differ by platform
queries: what field names does the basket use
productname vs item_name
svn1 svn2 what are they
basket format for my platform
why are my product names not showing
what keys go in the basket array
content:
The basket array uses different key names depending on how KST was installed. Copying a snippet from the wrong guide is a common cause of missing product data.

| Installation | Product name | Product ID | Quantity | Price |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Manual | `productname` | `productid` | `quantity` | `price` |
| PrestaShop 1.6 | `productname` | `productid` | `quantity` | `price` |
| PrestaShop 1.7 / 8 | `productname` | `productid` | `svn1` | `svn2` |
| Shopify | `productname` | `productid` | `quantity` | `price` |
| LightSpeed | `item_name` | `item_id` | `quantity` | `price` (plus `currency`) |
| GTM dataLayer | `name` | `sku` | `quantity` | `price` |
| Server-to-server | `productname` | `productid` | `quantity` | `price` |

Whichever form you use, the product identifier should match the ID in your Kelkoo Group offer feed — EAN, SKU or another unique product ID — so Kelkoo Group can match transactions to your feed. For server-to-server, `quantity` must be an integer; floating point is explicitly not allowed.

topic: General troubleshooting checklist across all platforms
queries: KST isn't tracking any sales what do I check
no conversions showing what should I check first
general troubleshooting checklist
zero sales in dashboard
it's just not working what do I do
my tracking is completely broken
the pixel never fires and no sales are recorded
where do I start debugging
content:
Patterns that recur across the GTM, PrestaShop and Shopify troubleshooting pages, ordered roughly by how often they are the cause:

1. **Not published / not deployed.** GTM containers must be published; PrestaShop caches must be cleared after edits.
2. **Both tags present?** Lead Tag on every page, Conversion Tag on the confirmation page. Missing either breaks attribution.
3. **Old tracking still installed.** Search for `leadtag.js` and `_kkstrack`, and remove obsolete LeGuide (`lgtrk`) code. Duplicates cause double or incorrect counting.
4. **Order values undefined or empty.** In GTM, check variables are not undefined in debug mode during a test sale; make sure the dataLayer sits above the GTM snippet, and use a *DOM ready* trigger if variables are declared after it.
5. **Syntax traps.** GTM variables need double brackets `{{like_this}}`, and straight quotes `"` not curly `“`. PrestaShop breaks if `{literal}` tags wrap the script (1.7/8) or are missing (1.6).
6. **Wrong file edited.** Especially on PrestaShop, where the correct template differs per version.
7. **Device- or section-specific placement.** On Shopify, a tag inside a mobile- or desktop-only section fires only for those users.
8. **Number formatting.** Shopify stores with non-default money formats mangle order values above 4 digits.
9. **Consent blocking the Lead Tag.** A CMP that suppresses it means no identifier is ever stored.
10. **Reinstall after upgrades.** Platform or theme updates overwrite the files the tags live in.

**A useful diagnostic signal:** if your Merchant Extranet shows the installation flipping between **V1 and V2**, that points at a tag firing inconsistently — on Shopify, a device-specific section; in GTM, a tag not on the DOM ready event.

Start with the Kelkoo Sales Tracking Debugging tool and the Installer's *Last Call Registered* view, which shows exactly what your pixel sent.

topic: Country code gotchas (uk not gb, nb for Flemish Belgium)
queries: is it uk or gb for the country code
what code for Belgium
what is nb country code
country code mistakes
my country code doesn't work
do I use ISO country codes
content:
Kelkoo Group's country codes mostly match the familiar 2-letter codes, with a few traps:

- **United Kingdom is `uk`, not `gb`.** `gb` is the ISO 3166 code and is *not* in Kelkoo's list.
- **Belgium has two entries**: `be` (Belgium) and `nb` (Flemish Belgium). `nb` is not a standard country code at all, so it is easy to miss when a store serves both language communities.
- Codes are always **lower case**.
- Each campaign has its own merchantId **and** country code pairing — running several countries means several merchantIds, configured together in the `merchantInfo` array.

The published list covers 38 countries. If a code you expect is absent, check the full list rather than assuming the ISO code works.

topic: Choosing between GTM, manual and server-to-server
queries: GTM or manual or server to server
which method is best for my site
should I use server to server
can I use more than one installation method
what are the trade-offs between installation methods
I specifically don't want GTM or a plugin what's left
content:
**Kelkoo Group's recommendation is GTM *and* server-to-server running in parallel**, to maximise coverage — not one or the other.

| | Best for | Requirements | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| **GTM** | Sites already using GTM with Enhanced Ecommerce | Good GTM knowledge | Official, recommended first choice |
| **Manual** | Any site where tags can go in the source | Development skills | Official; the fallback when GTM is unavailable and no platform guide exists |
| **Platform plugin** | WooCommerce, Unas | Little or none — plugin install | Simplest, where available |
| **Server-to-server** | Custom setups where browser tracking is unreliable | Advanced dev, in-house team, ~5 days minimum | **Fallback only** — explicitly not a replacement |

**Server-to-server carries documented limits worth stating plainly to anyone considering it:** Kelkoo Group provides no custom implementation and only very limited technical support for it; it requires an in-house development team and is not suitable for agencies or merchants without one; and it is intended to *increase coverage alongside* an official method, not to replace it.

If a merchant rules out both GTM and plugins, manual installation is the normal answer — server-to-server is a bigger commitment than most sites need.

queries: how do I run multiple Kelkoo campaigns
several merchant IDs one website
multi country tracking setup
I have campaigns in different countries
multi campaign configuration by platform
content:
Every installation method supports multi-campaign tracking. The mechanism is the same idea everywhere — one entry per campaign, each pairing a country with its merchantId — but where you configure it differs:

| Platform | Where to configure |
|---|---|
| Manual / Shopify / PrestaShop / LightSpeed | Add entries to the `merchantInfo` array in the Conversion Tag |
| WooCommerce | Plugin settings, using the Multi Merchant Information variable |
| Unas | Requires multiple languages set under Settings / Texts, Languages, then a merchantID per country |
| GTM | Configure in the Kelkoo tag template |

The array form used by the code-based platforms:

```
merchantInfo : [
  {
    country:'fr',
    merchantId:'12941513'
  },
  {
    country:'uk',
    merchantId:'56789'
  }
]
```

On PrestaShop 1.6 this array sits inside `{literal}...{/literal}` tags. Each merchantId comes with its own country code — find them together in the Merchant Extranet dropdown.

topic: What to re-check after a site, theme or platform update
queries: tracking stopped working after an update
do I need to redo the setup after upgrading
my sales disappeared after a site change
what breaks tracking when I redeploy
should I retest after changing my site
content:
KST installations live inside files that site updates routinely overwrite, so tracking can stop silently after otherwise routine work.

**Re-check after:**

- A **PrestaShop or theme upgrade** — the docs state KST must be reinstalled; upgrades replace `OrderConfirmationController.php` and the confirmation templates.
- A **Magento theme change** — the Lead Tag lives in theme layout XML.
- **Shopify theme edits** — a lead tag can end up inside a device-specific section.
- **Any CMP or cookie banner change** — the Lead Tag needs consent to store anything.
- **Any checkout or confirmation page redesign** — the Conversion Tag sits on that page.

**How to check quickly:** run a test purchase and look at *Last Call Registered* in the Kelkoo Sales Tracking Installer, which shows what the pixel actually sent. Then confirm the following day that the sale appears in Merchant Center Statistics with the right order value.

Kelkoo Group's own guidance is to check regularly that sales are still being registered, and especially after implementing updates or changes to your site.

topic: Where the Lead Tag and Conversion Tag go on each platform
queries: where do the tags go on my platform
which file do I edit for my platform
lead tag location by platform
quick reference for tag placement
what file holds the conversion tag
content:
Quick reference for where each tag lives, by installation method:

| Platform | Lead Tag | Conversion Tag |
|---|---|---|
| Manual | Before `</head>` on every page | Before `</body>` on the confirmation page |
| GTM | Custom HTML tag, trigger *All Pages* | Kelkoo template tag, trigger = purchase custom event |
| Shopify | Custom Pixel "Kelkoo Leadtag" (Settings → Customer Events) | Custom Pixel "Kelkoo Conversion", `checkout_completed` |
| WooCommerce | Handled by the plugin | Handled by the plugin |
| Unas | Handled by the plugin | Handled by the plugin |
| Magento 1 | XML layout, `<reference name="head">` | `checkout/success.phtml` |
| Magento 2 | `Magento_Theme/layout/default_head_blocks.xml` | Kelkoo module's `checkout/success.phtml` |
| PrestaShop 1.6 | `themes/custom/header.tpl` | `order-confirmation.tpl` + controller |
| PrestaShop 1.7 / 8 | `templates/_partials/head.tpl` | `checkout/_partials/order-confirmation-table.tpl` + controller |
| LightSpeed | Web Extras → Custom JavaScript | Web Extras → Tracking Code |
| Server-to-server | No browser tag — store `kk`/`gclid` server-side | HTTP GET to `https://s.kelkoogroup.net/st` |

The pattern is consistent: the Lead Tag goes somewhere loaded on *every* page, the Conversion Tag goes only where an order completes.
